chunks: Kurdawayh al-Hamdani asked Abū al-Ḥasan Mūsā ibn Jaʿfar عليه السلام.
About a well into which water from the road enters, containing urine, feces, the urine of beasts, their dung, and dog excrement.
So he said: “Thirty buckets are to be drawn from it, and if it is foul-smelling.”

key_terms.أَبْوَالُ الدَّوَابِّ: the urine of riding or pack animals
key_terms.الْبَوْلُ: urine as a source of impurity
key_terms.بِئْرٍ: a well used as a water source

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a well contaminated by urine, feces, and animal waste?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a fiqh ruling about a well contaminated by roadway runoff carrying various impurities. Imam Mūsā ibn Jaʿfar عليه السلام instructs that thirty buckets should be drawn from the well, including in the case that it has a foul odor.
